title: Advanced Gas Settings - Adjusting Transaction Fees in Metamask
description:
How to adjust Transaction Fees using Metamask whether for Forsage or simply transferring ETH to someone else.

- Gas Price and Limit is explained.
- Advanced Settings are explained
- Nonce Settings are shown but not completely explained...as that is for a different training.

asr.full_text: Hey everyone just want to do a quick video on how to adjust your transaction costs otherwise known as setting your gas fees so just start off by saying you do not have to be on the Versage site to be able to access your MetaMask wallet but anybody who opens The MetaMask wallet while other tabs are open just realize that those other tabs do have access to information about your wallet. So, just be careful and make sure you're not on a site that is unknown when you're opening up your wallet. Another quick note about MetaMask is if you do not see the little Fox icon in the upper right-hand corner of your browser window, then what you can do is click on the little puzzle symbol, the white puzzle symbol and that'll do a drop down and then you'll be able to press this button right here which will pin MettaMask to the top. And once you do that, it will appear at the top of your screen so you can get to it easily. So once you click on that then it'll give you a screen where you put in your password and you log in and if we're using an example of just sending money from from one wallet to another. In that case as opposed to starting a transaction from the for such site , you would enter a wallet address, you would enter the amount that you would like to transfer. Normally, you just pick whether you wanted to go slow average or fast speed and then you click next. But you may not have noticed that there's an advanced options here. So now if you click on advanced options that'll give you a lot more control over what the actual amount of gas is that you're going to pay for that transaction. So if we click on advanced you'll see it now shows gas price which is listed in GUI and the gas limit, both of which you can adjust. And once you adjust them, you'll click on the save button, but just real quick, let's explain what that is. So what is Gui? So the gas amount that they show you, the gas price, if you were to divide that by one billion that would actually give you the gas price in ether so 70 gui would end up being 0.000000 2007 ether so now this gas price just so you're aware is sort of like going to a gas station and fueling up your vehicle. There's a price on the billboard that says how much the the gas would cost. So a lot of people get confused and think that the gas price is what they're going to pay for the transaction fee. And that's simply not true. It's just the price. per gallon, so to speak. It's the price per usage within the ethereum network so if you take that amount that gas price and multiply that by how much gas your transaction actually requires to be processed since every transaction has processing time that's associated with it some are easier than others if you're registering for an x3 x4 level one there's multiple transactions going on and your total usage will be fairly high if you're registering in x gold for the first time the slot one or level one your usage amount will be higher than normal as you upgrade each level it may not require as much gas in order to move to the next level. If you're simply sending money from one wallet to another. Then that's a really simple process that's it's like driving less distance in a car. So this usage amount the actual amount that you use is sort of like the distance that you go, how many gallons or liters did you use, right of gas in order to refill your tank. So if you think about it in that way you multiply your actual gas price times the amount that's actually used, and that'll tell you how much a theory,ium it will take as a transaction fee. So if, in this example, we're using $70 Gui as the gas price. We actually had a usage of $399,878. That turns into a .02799, which if you're assuming $1,000 US per Ethereum, that would equate to $27.99 in dollars for that particular transaction fee. Now, what is the limit? Notice, the gas usage is up to a gas limit. The limit that you're setting is saying, I don't want to pay that gas price if the transaction takes more than a certain amount of of usage so for example in x Gold we're we're setting the gas limit to uh it was 700,000 or a million just to make sure that the transaction is able to use enough gas to complete without failing so when the system actually determines how much is actually used that will reset from your estimated gas amount to your actual gas amount the limit just says i don't want it to go over this so i don't want to drive more than X number of Miles in the car analogy. Once I get to that point I'm done. Whether I got to my destination or not. I've used my gas, so that is why you will still lose your you'll have a transaction fee associated with a transaction that fails. You still drove a certain distance before the transaction failed, and that is why you still are charged a gas amount. So the idea is to set your maximum as high as you need or want, but you have the ability to adjust the gas price down to an acceptable level. The difference there is it's like saying, okay, I'm willing to pay X amount for gas at the gas station. But the current price at the gas station is higher than I want to pay. So, I'm going to sit and wait before I refill my car until they dropped that price down. That's what you're doing when you adjust the gas price, you're saying to the gas station owner in this case, it's the miners who are running the Ethereum network, but to follow it, the analogy of refilling your tank after a trip, it's like sitting in front of that gas station and saying, I'm only gonna pay $2 for gas. So until you drop your price to two dollars i will sit here and wait and that's what happens when you drop your gas price below whatever the going rate is at the time that you want to put your transaction through if you set your gas price to higher than the going rate it's going to process almost immediately and you know you'll pay based upon how much usage times that gas price if you set the gas price to a lower amount then you set the weight for the price to drop so hopefully that helps clear up a little bit of the what are these different things but when you set those so here this example is showing you know 58 would be the gas price the gas limit is 21 000. so in this case it would not be able to do usage of more than 21 000 and then i would click save and then it comes back and shows what the transaction fee would be and then you would click next that'll take you to another screen which should look familiar because this is kind of the starting point when you're actually doing a for size transaction it jumps right to here with an ether amount of you know 0.05 for for level 1 as an example and that is where you know most people are just clicking confirm you do have the ability though to click on this edit button at that point and still get to the same level of control so when you click on edit it initially shows you a slow average fast speed transaction and how much each would cost but you'll notice at the top of that screen there is an advanced tab so you can go to the advanced tab change your gas price change your gas limit if you need to just make sure it's high enough and click save and then come back and hit confirm once it shows the new total that you're willing to pay for that transaction fee so now a little trick that will help you with this is under the circle in the upper right hand, there is a dropdown, and that drop down. There's a settings button. When you click on settings, one of the options is advanced. So if you click on the right arrow there, that'll take you to some additional settings that you have control over, and if you scroll down a bit, you'll see advanced gas controls now if you turn that setting on then every transaction from that point on by the way just click x to close this settings screen and you can come back and start another transaction you notice that the transaction fee settings are right there and you don't have to go to advanced at that point you can immediately just set your gas price set your gas limit and click on next you don't have to go into the advanced options the same is true on the the screen that you initially come to when this when a transaction is initiated by the Versage system it would have the appropriate amount of the Ethereum and then you can click on the Edit button and change it from there as well. Now, another setting underneath the circle in the upper right hand corner, you go to settings. If you scroll down inside of the advanced tab, even further, you'll come down to something called customize transaction nots. Now, in this case, when that is on and I close the screen, you'll notice there's a difference on the main screen of this custom nonce. So if anybody ever tells you, and that's a different training as to why you'd ever wanna set this nonce. But if anybody tells you, you know, to send say a $0 transaction to yourself to clear out a transaction, to cancel a transaction, then what you'll have to do is set your custom nonce to the same number as the nonce on the transaction that you're trying to clear. And that's how you can do that from METAMASK. And when you're done, you would click confirm just like normal, and that's all there is
